title: The Missing Layer: Design Taste in AI Agents — Hassan El Mghari, Together AI
talk_summary: A developer-experience lead describes how he gets non-slop UI out of coding agents by codifying 'AI slop' anti-patterns into a skill (Hallmark), feeding curated theme/reference screenshots as context, writing long specific prompts, and iterating with cheaper open-source models instead of expensive closed ones. The core transferable mechanism is a reusable markdown/skill file of negative constraints plus reference examples, and model-tiering by task phase.

takeaways.technique: Codified anti-pattern 'slop gates' in a skill file
takeaways.what_they_do: Enumerates concrete failure patterns (purple gradients, italic headers, all-caps pills, emoji spam, gradient logos) and bakes them as explicit 'don't do this' rules into a reusable skill the model loads as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: takes all of these uh AI slop patterns uh and uh codifies them uh and and tells AI models like hey like don't don't use these

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains a personal collection of good examples and pastes many screenshots into the prompt as context; claims output is consistently much better than without references.
takeaways.evidence_quote: please give your agents references and screenshots ... the output will always be way way way better

takeaways.technique: Cheap model for iteration, expensive model for base
takeaways.what_they_do: Starts a project with a strong closed model to establish the base, then does the many follow-up iteration prompts with a cheaper, faster open-source model, arguing the quality gap is often indistinguishable for iteration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of the apps that I build now I'll kind of start in like codec or cloud code to build a base and then for iterating I'll use usually smaller open source model
takeaways.numbers: claims the closed-model page 'cost five times as much and was a lot slower'

takeaways.technique: Long, specific prompts + one-to-two features per step
takeaways.what_they_do: Writes 2-3 paragraph prompts (often dictated as voice notes) covering users, layout, and constraints, and splits multi-feature work into separate sequential prompts rather than one mega-prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're building seven different features, you probably don't want to put them all in the same prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: As he notices recurring model mistakes, he appends rules to an agent.md so the same correction isn't re-typed each session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can start to build out an agent.mmd that has a bunch of this stuff like avoid this for the logo

takeaways.technique: Queue follow-up iteration prompts up front
takeaways.what_they_do: After the initial big prompt, he immediately queues a series of smaller follow-up messages (one feature each) and lets the agent run through them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: immediately I'll queue up like a bunch of other messages of like oh we'll do this feature and do this feature
